title: design_report — the sidecar written beside design_context.json
description: Design-process feedback and the extraction's own conservation proof. Kept out of design_context.json because that file is consumed for screens, elements and flow, while these are tallies about how the board was authored. Written as <design_context>.report.json. Downstream: sdet-plan-generator renders the Design Convention Compliance table from it, and check_design_context.py verifies conservation against it — an absent sidecar makes those checks report SKIPPED, never silently pass.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the extraction run.

design_context_file.description: Name of the design_context this report describes, so a stray sidecar cannot be paired with the wrong context.

convention_compliance.description: Tallies of how well the export follows the design team's flow-authoring conventions — the feedback loop back to design. connectors_total must equal the sum of the six connector buckets; a shortfall means connectors were dropped silently, which is the failure this block exists to make impossible.

connectors_total.description: Every CONNECTOR node in the export.

connectors_resolved_to_screen.description: Both endpoints resolved to screens (standard #1 followed).

connectors_inferred_to_screen.description: Destination was an element, a lane caption or a label frame; the screen was inferred.

connectors_unresolvable.description: Floating endpoint, orphaned node id, or a destination with no board-node ancestor. Each is also a blocking_issues entry.

connectors_intra_screen.description: Both endpoints inside the same screen (including two state-frames of one screen) — a state transition or annotation, not navigation.

connectors_to_decision.description: Connectors terminating on a DECISION box. Each is consumed by contraction, which emits one edge per labelled exit — so this is its own bucket, not part of connectors_resolved_to_screen.

note_connectors.description: Either endpoint (or an ancestor of it) is an annotation component or Note/Context text.

caption_endpoints.description: Connectors landing on a CAPTION / LANE_BANNER rather than a screen.

label_frames_resolved.description: Connectors rescued by the label-frame fallback: the destination was a gibberish-named strip that proved to be the label of exactly one column-aligned screen below it. Fires only on a resolution failure, never as a sweep.

connector_direction_flipped.description: Connectors whose arrowhead points at connectorStart, meaning the flow runs opposite to the direction the line was drawn. The edge is emitted in the arrowhead's direction and stamped edge_direction_source: ARROWHEAD_REVERSED. Non-zero is worth telling design: the line reads backwards on the board.

decision_nodes.description: Board nodes classified DECISION — a small question box with 2+ outgoing connectors.

contracted_edges.description: Edges emitted by collapsing a decision box (edge_source CONNECTOR_CONTRACTED). Far above connectors_total means contraction escaped its one-hop / fan-out bounds and is manufacturing flows.

lane_entry_inferred.description: Edges whose destination is a lane's entry screen picked by reading order rather than stated.

reactions_with_destination.description: Prototype NODE actions naming a destination, whatever the navigation type.

reactions_destination_outside_export.description: Of those, the ones whose destination is not in this export — usually a component variant in a library, so the link cannot be followed from here.

reactions_without_destination.description: Tap-family triggers (ON_CLICK / ON_PRESS / ON_DRAG / ON_KEY_DOWN) with a null or absent destination (standard #2 not followed). Non-tap triggers such as AFTER_TIMEOUT are excluded — a timeout without a destination is not the same authoring mistake.

unlabelled_branches.description: A trigger element with 2+ outgoing connectors and no labels to discriminate them (standard #4 not followed).

non_descriptive_names.description: Screens still named Frame 427, Group 12 etc after the banner-rename fallback ran (standard #3 not followed).

screen_id_from_banner.description: Screens whose gibberish name was replaced by the text of the section banner above them. Each rename moves a join key, so each is also a DEGRADED gap in design_context.

unreachable_screens.description: Screens in no ui_flow edge and no flowStartingPoints entry.

notes_total.description: NOTE-classified board nodes found. The three notes_* buckets must sum to this; a shortfall means note text was dropped silently.

notes_attached_by_connector.description: Notes routed by an explicit connector to the screen or element they describe (standard #5 followed).

notes_attached_by_geometry.description: Notes with no connector, attached to the screen containing them or nearest within the same parent. Inferred, not drawn.

notes_unattached.description: Notes belonging to no screen — outside every frame and with no connector. Reported as one INFO gap, never a blocker.

state_labels_attached.description: Label chips/bars proactively attached to the screen they name (v2 exports): states drawn as separate frames under a label, recovered without any connector. Includes arrow_bound_labels.

arrow_bound_labels.description: Of state_labels_attached, those bound by a hand-drawn LINE arrow from label to screen — explicit binding, stronger than column alignment.

label_attach_conflicts.description: Labels aligning with 2+ screens, or dashed group boxes surrounding screens with distinct proper names. Each is a blocking_issues entry; never guessed.

group_box_clusters.description: Dashed board-level boxes that merged >=2 sibling screen groups into one screen (v2 exports). Details in group_box_merges.

fingerprint_merged_frames.description: Default-named frames collapsed into sibling screens by shared component skeleton (Jaccard >= 0.8). Structural inference — every merge is also a DEGRADED extraction gap. Details in fingerprint_merges.

section_entry_inferred.description: Connectors drawn into a SECTION (no board-node ancestor) resolved to that section's entry screen — the lane-banner semantic expressed with an explicit container. Part of connectors_inferred_to_screen.

ambiguous_collapses.description: Collapsed screens (>=2 frames) where no qualifier reads as a state — possibly distinct screens sharing a generic base name. Each is a blocking_issues entry; the collapse is kept, never silently split.

screen_renames.description: Every screen_id replaced by a banner name, so a QA holding an older plan can re-map. Empty when nothing was renamed.

group_box_merges.description: Audit trail for every dashed-group-box merge: which box, which screen ids were absorbed into which.

fingerprint_merges.description: Audit trail for every fingerprint merge of default-named sibling frames — auditable and challengeable, unlike a silent collapse.

unclassified_states.description: screen_states entries whose text maps to no canonical state_kind (feature-specific labels, non-English copy). The post-run model pass normalises each into the state_kinds enum or leaves it, with the source text kept verbatim in screen_states.
